details: The United States and China have reached an agreement to reduce tariffs on $30 billion worth of goods and establish a formal dialogue on artificial intelligence. This development follows President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington, signaling efforts to stabilize bilateral relations and cooperation. The tariff reductions are expected to apply to various non-sensitive goods.
title: China, US agree to AI dialogue, tariff cuts on $30 billion in goods

details: The U.S. Transportation Department is set to finalize significantly lower vehicle fuel economy standards through 2031. This decision reverses a previous push by the Biden administration to accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles. Officials indicate the move aims to reduce the cost of new vehicles, though it is projected to increase fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions over decades.
title: US to finalize sharply lower vehicle fuel economy standards

details: S&P 500 earnings per share saw a substantial 51% surge in the second quarter, with Goldman Sachs estimating that nearly half of 2026's earnings growth is attributable to spending on artificial intelligence. However, the investment bank cautions that this pace of AI-driven growth may not be sustainable, and the depreciation from hyperscaler capital expenditures could largely offset these gains by 2028.
title: AI Boom Drives S&P 500 Profits, But Tailwind Fading

details: The Federal Reserve is reportedly planning to propose the reindexing of thresholds that determine more stringent capital, stress testing, and liquidity requirements for larger banks. This adjustment would account for economic growth and inflation, potentially raising the lowest threshold from $100 billion in assets to around $150 billion, and the highest threshold closer to $1 trillion.
title: Fed Plans to Reindex Bank Capital, Liquidity Thresholds
